# Sources and trade-offs

The research behind `ui-states`, and where its rules deliberately differ from common guidance.

## Sources

**Response time and progress**

- Nielsen Norman Group, [Response times: the 3 important limits](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/response-times-3-important-limits/): 0.1 s feels instant, 1 s keeps the flow of thought, 10 s holds attention; past 10 s, show progress and an estimate.
- Nielsen Norman Group, [Progress indicators make a slow system less insufferable](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/progress-indicators/): an indicator for any action over about 1 s; a looped indicator for 2 to 10 s, a percent-done indicator past about 10 s; people wait longer and are more satisfied when they see dynamic progress.
- Nielsen Norman Group, [Skeleton screens 101](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/skeleton-screens/): a wireframe-like placeholder that mimics the page's layout and reduces perceived load time; static-content, animated and frame-display kinds; for waits under 10 s; under 1 s, neither a skeleton nor a spinner is needed.
- Nielsen Norman Group, [Indicators, validations and notifications](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/indicators-validations-notifications/): status shown in context, notifications for events away from it.
- Material Design 3, [Progress indicators](https://m3.material.io/components/progress-indicators/guidelines): determinate when the amount is known, indeterminate otherwise.
- Apple Human Interface Guidelines, [Progress indicators](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/progress-indicators) and [Feedback](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/feedback): prefer determinate progress, keep indicators moving, describe the work, and give feedback in place.
- Microsoft Fluent 2, [Spinner](https://fluent2.microsoft.design/components/web/react/core/spinner/usage) and [ProgressBar](https://fluent2.microsoft.design/components/web/react/core/progressbar/usage).
- Carbon, [Inline loading](https://carbondesignsystem.com/components/inline-loading/usage/): an inline spinner in place of what it replaces, with active, finished and error states; the success state stays 1.5 s; interactive elements tied to the button are disabled while it loads. Carbon, [Loading pattern](https://carbondesignsystem.com/patterns/loading-pattern/).

**Saving and inline feedback**

- GitHub Primer, [Saving](https://primer.style/product/ui-patterns/saving/) and [Loading](https://primer.style/product/ui-patterns/loading/) patterns: start with explicit saving; never mix automatic and explicit saving in one form; keep the person's data in the form when a save fails; prefer explicit saving for text inputs, checkbox and radio groups and selects, because arrow keys and screen readers can select an option just by reading it.
- Material Design 3, [Switch](https://m3.material.io/components/switch/guidelines) and [Text fields](https://m3.material.io/components/text-fields/guidelines): a switch toggles one item on or off; a field shows its error state in its outline and supporting text.
- Fluent 2, [Field](https://fluent2.microsoft.design/components/web/react/core/field/usage): validation messages tied to the field, with success, warning and error states.

**Notifications**

- Material Design 3, [Snackbar](https://m3.material.io/components/snackbar/guidelines): short updates about a process at the bottom of the screen that disappear after a timeout or stay until the person acts, optionally with one action such as Undo or Retry ([Android component docs](https://github.com/material-components/material-components-android/blob/master/docs/components/Snackbar.md)).
- Fluent 2, [Toast](https://fluent2.microsoft.design/components/web/react/core/toast/usage): confirmation, progress and communication toasts; with no action to take, a toast times out after seven seconds, and hovering pauses the timer; conditional dismissal for progress; a close button only when the content can be found again elsewhere; never for critical messages (use a message bar or a dialog). Fluent 2, [MessageBar](https://fluent2.microsoft.design/components/web/react/core/messagebar/usage).
- Atlassian, [Flag](https://atlassian.design/components/flag/usage): bottom left of the screen, the most recent on top of a stack; never auto-dismiss a critical warning or error; never mix dismissible and non-dismissible flags in one stack; avoid dead ends. Atlassian, [Banner](https://atlassian.design/components/banner/usage) and [Inline message](https://atlassian.design/components/inline-message/usage).
- Carbon, [Notifications pattern](https://carbondesignsystem.com/patterns/notification-pattern/): task-generated notifications in the region the person is working in; toasts without actions may auto-dismiss, toasts with actions persist until dismissed; banners for system-level states.
- GitHub Primer, [Notification messaging](https://primer.style/product/ui-patterns/notification-messaging/): banners and inline messages for feedback near the action; for toast-like needs it points to its accessibility guidance on alternatives to toasts.
- Shopify Polaris, [Toast API](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/app-home/latest/apis/user-interface-and-interactions/toast-api) and [Banner](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/app-home/latest/web-components/feedback-and-status-indicators/banner): short, non-critical confirmations versus persistent, actionable messages.

**Errors**

- Nielsen Norman Group, [Error-message guidelines](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/error-message-guidelines/): visible near the problem, in plain words, constructive, preserving input.
- Nielsen Norman Group, [10 usability heuristics](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/ten-usability-heuristics/): H1 visibility of system status, H5 error prevention, H9 recognise, diagnose and recover from errors.
- Apple Human Interface Guidelines, [Alerts](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/alerts): use sparingly, for important information that needs a decision.
- Carbon, [Notification](https://carbondesignsystem.com/components/notification/usage/) and Polaris, [Banner](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/app-home/latest/web-components/feedback-and-status-indicators/banner): inline and section-level errors with an action.

**Accessibility**

- WCAG 2.2, [4.1.3 Status messages](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages.html): the result of an action, a waiting state, progress and the existence of errors, presented by assistive technology without receiving focus.
- WCAG 2.2, [2.2.1 Timing adjustable](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/timing-adjustable.html): time limits can be turned off, adjusted or extended; its own example says a toast that disappears sets no time limit when its information is available another way, which is why the pill is never the only home of anything.
- WCAG 2.2, [1.4.1 Use of color](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color.html), [1.4.11 Non-text contrast](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-contrast.html), [2.3.3 Animation from interactions](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/animation-from-interactions.html), [3.3.1 Error identification](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/error-identification.html), [3.3.3 Error suggestion](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/error-suggestion.html).
- WAI-ARIA, [`aria-busy`](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2/#aria-busy), [`status` role](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2/#status) (polite), [`alert` role](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2/#alert) (assertive), [`aria-disabled`](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2/#aria-disabled); MDN, [`aria-disabled`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-disabled): it doesn't change focusability, so the control stays in the tab order and the author suppresses its input; the APG [Alert pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/alert/): alerts never move focus, shouldn't disappear on their own, and interrupt, so use them sparingly. MDN, [ARIA live regions](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Guides/Live_regions): a live region must be in the page before the change it announces.
- MDN, [`prefers-reduced-motion`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@media/prefers-reduced-motion).

**Optimistic and pessimistic updates, and flicker**

- React, [`useOptimistic`](https://react.dev/reference/react/useOptimistic): show the expected result at once and fall back when the action fails.
- The delay-before-showing and minimum-display patterns behind `perceived-performance`'s 300 ms delay and 500 ms minimum: an indicator that appears and vanishes within a few hundred milliseconds reads as a glitch.

**Shimmer (skeleton) loading**

- Fluent 2, [Skeleton](https://fluent2.microsoft.design/components/web/react/core/skeleton/usage): for content that takes over a second when its structure is known (a spinner or bar when it isn't); wave (default) or pulse animation kept in sync across placeholders; simultaneous data calls to avoid staggered loading; reflect consistent, high-level structure, not details; `aria-busy` while loading and a polite live region only for important blocks.
- Carbon, [Loading pattern](https://carbondesignsystem.com/patterns/loading-pattern/): skeleton states for container and data components (tiles, lists, tables, cards), never for buttons, inputs, toggles, menus, toasts or the modal itself; motion shows the page isn't stuck; they should last only a few seconds; progressive loading puts the structure first, then content in batches.
- GitHub Primer, [Loading](https://primer.style/product/ui-patterns/loading/), [SkeletonText](https://primer.style/product/components/skeleton-text/) and [SkeletonBox](https://primer.style/product/components/skeleton-box/): a content skeleton for large loading areas, a spinner beside a message otherwise; animation subtle and sparing; no loading state under about 1 s; determinate progress past about 3 s; background tasks past 10 s.
- Shopify Polaris, [Skeleton page](https://github.com/Shopify/polaris/blob/main/polaris.shopify.com/content/components/feedback-indicators/skeleton-page.mdx) and [Skeleton body text](https://github.com/Shopify/polaris/blob/main/polaris.shopify.com/content/components/feedback-indicators/skeleton-body-text.mdx): mimic the layout that will load; a known title stays real while dynamic parts are skeletons; for pages whose content loads at once.
- Material Design 3, [Progress indicators](https://m3.material.io/components/progress-indicators/guidelines): the spinner and bar side of the choice, determinate when the amount is known.
- WCAG 2.2, [2.2.2 Pause, stop, hide](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/pause-stop-hide.html): moving content that starts automatically, lasts more than 5 s and sits alongside other content needs a way to pause, stop or hide it; a preload animation can count as essential, but a finite shimmer doesn't need the exception. MDN, [`forced-colors`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@media/forced-colors).

**Empty states**

- Nielsen Norman Group, [Designing empty states in complex applications](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/empty-state-interface-design/): a totally empty container leaves people unsure whether it's loading, failed or filtered out; use empty states to show system status, teach, and offer a direct path to the key task.
- Material Design 2, [Empty states](https://m2.material.io/design/communication/empty-states.html): its communication guidance on what a container shows when it has no content.
- GitHub Primer, [Empty states](https://primer.style/product/ui-patterns/empty-states/) and [Blankslate](https://primer.style/product/components/blankslate/): different primary text for never used, temporarily empty and failed; one primary action; error empty states never playful.
- Carbon, [Empty states pattern](https://carbondesignsystem.com/patterns/empty-states-pattern/): no-data, user-action (no results, completion) and error-management types; empty states appear in the space of the missing content; quiet actions when several show at once; text only when space is short; an empty table's state replaces the table so a screen reader doesn't read its headers first.
- Atlassian, [Empty state](https://atlassian.design/components/empty-state/usage): for a new board, a cleared inbox or no search results; a header, a reason and what to do next; one call to action; illustrations neutral or humorous, never negative, alt text only when meaningful.
- Shopify Polaris, [Empty state](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/app-home/latest/web-components/feedback-and-status-indicators/empty-state): says why a page, list or table has nothing and what to do; inside a table it spans every column; for empty lists, empty tables, unconfigured features and filtered results.
- Fluent 2, [Skeleton](https://fluent2.microsoft.design/components/web/react/core/skeleton/usage): skeletons hint at structure for loads over a second, animate (wave or pulse) and use `aria-busy`; Fluent 2 has no dedicated empty-state component.
- web.dev, [Cumulative layout shift](https://web.dev/articles/cls): reserve space so content arriving doesn't move what's around it.
- WCAG 2.2, [1.1.1 Non-text content](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-content.html): decorative images are hidden from assistive technology.

## Where these rules differ from common guidance

| Rule here | Common guidance | Why the rule stands, and its cost |
|---|---|---|
| A committed change shows pending at once for at least 200 ms, then confirmed for at least 200 ms, even when the save is instant | Show nothing for actions under about 1 s (NN/g, Primer), or delay indicators about 300 ms, so nothing flickers | Flicker is an indicator of unpredictable length. A fixed beat that always ends in a tick reads as "done", and it answers "did that save?", which a silent instant save leaves open. Each half holds the beat, so a switch's spinner never shows for a single frame. The cost: about 400 ms of feedback for an instant save, of which at most 200 ms locks that one control. Loads and redraws keep the delay. |
| Single values save on their own (blur-commit) with the 200 ms confirmation, beside explicit Save for values that belong together | Primer: start with explicit saving, and prefer it for text inputs, checkbox and radio groups and selects | Settings that stand alone shouldn't need a Save button the person hunts for; the confirmation answers Primer's worry that a person can't tell whether it saved. Primer's other risks are handled: a radio group, a native select and a slider moved by arrow keys commit when focus leaves them or after a pause, never on each arrow press; sensitive values (a password, anything that's hard to take back) always use explicit save; and the two patterns never mix in one section. |
| A field is momentarily locked while it saves | Never block input (`perceived-performance`) | The lock covers only the committed control, after its edit ended (blur), for the beat or the save, with the element kept focusable (`aria-disabled`, never unmounted); the rest of the app stays usable, so no typing is lost. Continuous text (a document, a long description) is never locked: it autosaves while the person types, with its state in the status line. |
| A switch shows a spinner, then the new value (pessimistic) | Many products flip a switch optimistically and roll it back on failure | The value shown is the stored value: no switch is shown on that later turns out off. The 200 ms floor keeps it quick. Structural list actions (delete, move, reorder) stay optimistic, with Undo or rollback. |
| The notification pill allows three lines in exceptional cases | Toasts and snackbars are kept short (Polaris: quick, short feedback; Fluent: useful but never critical) | A partial success or an error's reason sometimes needs the count and the cause together; one line stays the norm, and more goes behind Details. |
| A global toast-like pill exists at all | Primer steers toast-like feedback to banners, inline messages and dialogs | The pill is never the only home of anything essential, errors don't auto-dismiss, timers pause and can be turned off, and in-place states come first. |
| Step text may use technical step names | `ui-copy`: no developer words before the person chooses them | The step line is subtle and fleeting; its job is to show steady life, which specific, fast-changing names do best. Headlines, errors and buttons still follow `ui-copy`. |
| A "Saved" label holds about 1.5 s | Carbon's success state: 1.5 s | Compatible: 200 ms is the floor for any confirmation; words need reading time (`duration.confirm-read`). |
| A shimmer skeleton shows after 300 ms and its motion stops after a few passes | Primer and NN/g: no loading state under about 1 s; Fluent: skeletons for loads over a second; Carbon: skeleton motion shows the page isn't stuck; WCAG 2.2.2 lets a preload animation count as essential | 300 ms is `perceived-performance`'s delay for every load indicator, and the 500 ms minimum keeps it from flashing, so a load of 300 ms to 1 s shows a brief, stable skeleton instead of a blank region. Stopping after about 4.5 s keeps motion within WCAG 2.2.2 without relying on the exception; after that, the status words and the 10 s message show the page isn't stuck. |
| An empty state keeps the content's wrapper at its minimum size | Carbon: the empty state replaces the element (an empty table loses its headers) | The wrapper (frame, heading, toolbar, filters) stays so the layout holds and the way out stays in reach; what's inside is replaced. Column headers stay only when sorting or filtering makes them useful, and the message comes first in reading order either way. |
| A silhouette of the expected content | Most systems use an illustration or icon | A silhouette previews the real shape and costs no illustration; it must be static, faint and paired with words so it's never read as a loading skeleton. Illustrations remain fine at view and app scope. |
| A quirky message when there's nothing else to say | Primer and Atlassian: playful only where it fits, never for errors | Same limit here: playful only for first use, cleared and all-done states, never for no results, no access or failures, and never instead of a reason. |
| Several pills queue: at most three visible, errors first, auto-dismiss timers start only when visible | Atlassian: never mix dismissible and non-dismissible flags in one stack | The pill keeps one place and one shape, so a queue is needed when outcomes coincide. Mixing is safe because no pill is hidden while its timer runs, errors move to the front, and the count of waiting pills is shown. |
| A spinner replaces a switch, and a lock never drops focus | Carbon: disable the triggering control while it loads | "Replaces" is visual: the same focusable element stays in place with `aria-disabled`, because the `disabled` attribute or unmounting it drops keyboard focus to the start of the page. |
| The green tick has a spoken twin | A success icon is often decorative only | A tick is a non-colour cue for sighted people but says nothing to a screen reader; a polite, named announcement ("Project name saved") makes the confirmation reach everyone, coalesced so a run of commits isn't chatty. |
